title: Counit characterization of the inverse proper relative Künneth map
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-sf-kv-maps], and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Use its geometric six-functor datum on the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$, with the specified ordinary adjunctions $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$ and counits $\varepsilon_u$ of [fix-prop-adjunctions](1), the exchange and counit-defined projection maps of [def-exchange-projection], and the proper compact-support identifications $Ru_!\cong Ru_*$ of [prop-functor-package](3). Let $B,X,Y$ be separated finite-type schemes over $k$, let $f:X\to B$ and $g:Y\to B$ be proper $k$-morphisms, and let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Put $T=X\times_BY$, with projections $p:T\to X$, $q:T\to Y$, and $t=fp=gq$. Let
$$\kappa_{f,g}:Rt_!(Lp^*M\otimes_A^L Lq^*N)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!M\otimes_A^L Rg_!N$$
be exactly the canonical relative Künneth map of [thm-sf-kunneth-relative], built from composition, the two inverse projection maps and inverse compact-support exchange. Through the specified proper identifications $Ru_!=Ru_*$, put
$$\Pi_{f,g}=\kappa_{f,g}^{-1}:Rf_*M\otimes_A^L Rg_*N\longrightarrow Rt_*(Lp^*M\otimes_A^L Lq^*N).$$
Then its ordinary $Lt^*\dashv Rt_*$ transpose is
$$\varepsilon_t\circ Lt^*\Pi_{f,g}=Lp^*\varepsilon_{f,M}\otimes_A^L Lq^*\varepsilon_{g,N}.$$
The equality uses the canonical monoidal pullback comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] and the pullback composition identifications
$$Lt^*(Rf_*M\otimes_A^L Rg_*N)\cong Lp^*Lf^*Rf_*M\otimes_A^L Lq^*Lg^*Rg_*N.$$
In particular this formula concerns the specified inverse relative product map, not an arbitrary isomorphism between its source and target.

source.place: Evaluation (1), the claim: inverse relative Künneth composite is adjoint to the tensor of the two counits

proof.text: All the following calculations are at the fixed finite coefficient ring $A$, and $u^*,u_*,\otimes$ abbreviate $Lu^*,Ru_*,\otimes_A^L$. The maps $p,q$ are base changes of the proper maps $g,f$, and $t=gq$ is proper, by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a),(b) (Stacks Tags 01W3, 01W4). Thus [prop-functor-package](3) supplies the proper identifications for $f,g,p,q,t$. By [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i)--(iv), all the pullbacks, tensors and direct images used below remain in $D^b_{ctf}$. In particular put $F=f_*M$, $G=g_*N$, $H=p^*M$, and $Z=H\otimes q^*N$. By [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence], the compact-support exchange $b:g^*F\to q_*H$ is the ordinary exchange. By [fix-prop-projection-formula], the compact-support projection maps for $q,g$ identify with the direct-image projection maps $\pi_q,\pi_g$ defined in [def-exchange-projection]. These are identifications of the specified transformations, not choices of new isomorphisms.

source.place: Evaluation (1), paragraph beginning Indeed Ku_!: expand the relative product and its ordinary adjoint

proof.text:
Use throughout the natural monoidal and pullback-composition comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] and the adjunction-compatible composition convention of [fix-prop-adjunctions](3). Let $c:g_*q_*\xrightarrow{\sim}t_*$ be this direct-image comparison, read through the specified proper identifications. Write $\sigma$ for signed tensor symmetry and set
$$a=g_*(\sigma_{N,g^*F})\circ\pi_{g;N,F}\circ\sigma_{F,G}:F\otimes G\longrightarrow g_*(g^*F\otimes N),$$
$$d=\pi_{q;H,N}\circ(b\otimes1_N):g^*F\otimes N\longrightarrow q_*Z.$$
Reverse the defining composite in [thm-sf-kunneth-relative]: the final symmetry becomes $\sigma_{F,G}$, inverse projection for $g$ becomes $\pi_g$, inverse exchange becomes $b$, and inverse projection for $q$ becomes $\pi_q$. Naturality of tensor symmetry rewrites the intermediate $N\otimes q_*H$ as $q_*H\otimes N$. Consequently the specified inverse is exactly
$$\Pi_{f,g}=c_Z\circ g_*d\circ a.$$
This simply reverses the named arrows of the defining Künneth composite; compatibility with the proper identifications is part of the cited relative theorem.

proof.text:
Apply Step 3 at $(g,N,F)$. Naturality of $\varepsilon_g$ moves the postcomposition $g_*\sigma$ in $a$ outside the transpose. Compatibility of the pullback tensor comparison with signed symmetry [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] then gives
$$\varepsilon_{g,g^*F\otimes N}\circ g^*a
=\sigma_{N,g^*F}\circ(\varepsilon_{g,N}\otimes1_{g^*F})\circ\sigma_{g^*F,g^*G}
=1_{g^*F}\otimes\varepsilon_{g,N}.$$
The last equality is naturality of symmetry followed by $\sigma\circ\sigma=1$. Thus the two swaps introduce no residual sign. For the arrow $d$ of Step 2, counit naturality now reads
$$\varepsilon_{g,q_*Z}\circ g^*(g_*d\circ a)=d\circ(1_{g^*F}\otimes\varepsilon_{g,N}).$$

source.place: Evaluation (1), paragraph beginning Indeed Ku_!: expand the relative product and its ordinary adjoint

proof.text:
The composite-counit formula of [fix-prop-adjunctions](3), under $t^*=q^*g^*$ and $c$, is
$$\varepsilon_{t,Z}\circ t^*c_Z=\varepsilon_{q,Z}\circ q^*\varepsilon_{g,q_*Z}.$$
Substitute Step 2 and then Step 4. Functoriality gives the transpose of the specified inverse as
$$\varepsilon_{t,Z}\circ t^*\Pi_{f,g}
=\varepsilon_{q,Z}\circ q^*d\circ q^*(1_{g^*F}\otimes\varepsilon_{g,N}).$$
Apply Step 3 at $(q,H,N)$ and substitute the definition of $d$:
$$\varepsilon_{q,Z}\circ q^*d
=(\varepsilon_{q,H}\otimes1_{q^*N})\circ(q^*b\otimes1_{q^*N})
=(\varepsilon_{q,H}\circ q^*b)\otimes1_{q^*N}.$$
All displayed tensor identifications and their naturality use [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso].

source.place: Evaluation (1), paragraph beginning Indeed Ku_!: expand the relative product and its ordinary adjoint

proof.text:
The exchange $b:g^*f_*M\to q_*p^*M$ is the mate of the pullback square, so [def-exchange-projection] (equivalently [fix-prop-adjunctions](4)) states its transpose exactly:
$$\varepsilon_{q,H}\circ q^*b=p^*\varepsilon_{f,M}$$
after $q^*g^*\cong p^*f^*$. Substitute this in Step 5. Naturality of the monoidal comparison [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identifies $q^*(1\otimes\varepsilon_{g,N})$ with $1\otimes q^*\varepsilon_{g,N}$; the tensor interchange law gives
$$\varepsilon_{t,Z}\circ t^*\Pi_{f,g}
=(p^*\varepsilon_{f,M}\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes q^*\varepsilon_{g,N})
=p^*\varepsilon_{f,M}\otimes q^*\varepsilon_{g,N}.$$
This has source $p^*f^*f_*M\otimes q^*g^*g_*N$ and target $Z$, exactly the source and target in the statement after its specified comparisons. It proves the asserted equality for $\kappa_{f,g}^{-1}$ itself, because Step 2 identified that particular map before taking its transpose.
